     manual approval.
-->

## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bug Fix
- [ ] Optimization
- [ ] Documentation Update

## Description

A user can now report abuse in Connect. Most of this work was done in #11332. I'm just closing the loop on this.

![A screenshot of the new report abuse feature in Connect](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104380977-d6119b00-54f9-11eb-9e4f-1114a9bccee2.png)

![A screenshot of the new report abuse feature in Connect](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104378932-b88f0200-54f6-11eb-9914-f223ba5d85ae.png)

One question I have @citizen428 since I don't know what the original specs were for this was. You can report a message, but if you try to report a second message from that user, it says that an abuse submission has already been filed. Is this how the implementation should work? I understand if they block the user as well that maybe it doesn't make sense to report another message, but when just reporting the message, I'm not sure.

## Related Tickets & Documents

This builds off the work in #11332. 

## QA Instructions, Screenshots, Recordings

1. Log in as the development mode main admin (email: admin@forem.local, password: password)
2. Make the main admin a tag moderator, for example, for the discuss tag, http://localhost:3000/admin/tags/13/edit
	1. Add the main admin as a tag moderator (their ID is 11)
	2. Click the Add Moderator button to apply the change. (This is required to be able to create new channels)
	3. Go back to Connect, localhost:3000/connect
	4. Create a channel and invite a user to the channel by clicking on the <kbd>+</kbd> icon.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350182-de55e000-54d1-11eb-972e-659eeb11f70b.png)

	5. The create channel modal will open. Enter a channel name and the username of another user to invite.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350218-e9a90b80-54d1-11eb-8efb-558137117722.png)

	6. In the newly created channel, create a message.
1. In another browser (private browser mode or a different browser), log on as the other user. All test users have a password of password. If you need to find the users email address to logon, go into the rails console and search for that user.
2. Once logged on as the other user. Accept the invitation to the new connect channel by clicking on the people icon with a badge notification.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350182-de55e000-54d1-11eb-972e-659eeb11f70b.png)

3. In the chat channel, hover over the message of the other user. The three dots contextual menu will appear. Hover over it to report abuse.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350312-05141680-54d2-11eb-881a-89cb46fcba68.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350347-0d6c5180-54d2-11eb-8ac6-ee0e1d83ba5b.png)

4. Select an abuse option. This is required to submit the form. Otherwise the report message button will stay disabled.
5. Click on the report message button. A confirmation window will notify you that the message will be reported and it will also ask you if you’d like to block the user.
	1. If you choose to block the user, the message will be reported and the user will be blocked from interacting with you on the platform.
	2. If you choose not to block the user, only the message will be reported.
6. Note, if you try to report a message from that user again, you will be notified that the report has already been submitted.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350389-1826e680-54d2-11eb-82e0-1e91faddd5b6.png)

### UI accessibility concerns?

The three dot contextual menu is not accessible. However, I filed is a separate issue, #12250, as this is more of a global issue in Connect.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104382321-e591e380-54fb-11eb-8ace-d54c2a09b20f.png)

For this feature, the report abuse panel works fine with keyboard navigation and has focus styles. For the radio buttons we're using the [focus visible polyfill](https://www.npmjs.com/package/focus-visible).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350920-b6b34780-54d2-11eb-879a-7cab1468cece.png)

The report message button appears to be using the default browser styles. This could be something to improve upon for our button component. cc: @lisasy @ludwiczakpawel.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/833231/104350988-cdf23500-54d2-11eb-860d-65770298e98b.png)

Also screenshare from #11332 

![Screen Recording 2020-11-09 at 11 35 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3650216/98505988-87891b80-2280-11eb-9da0-cfdb9bbfd38b.gif)

## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Feature
- [X] Bug Fix
- [ ] Optimization
- [ ] Documentation Update

## Description

In Connect, the message options menu (the three dots at the right) previously appeared only on hover, and was inaccessible for keyboard and assistive technology users. This PR makes sure those buttons are 'real' buttons which become visible on focus as well as hover.

Other accessibility features have been added also, namely:

- The buttons are identified as having a popup with an expanded state
- The menus can be opened on keyboard Enter press as well as click
- The menus can be dismissed with the Escape key
- When opened, focus is transferred directly to the first item in the list
- When closed, focus is transferred back to the button which opened the menu
- Where the dropdown had two items, they've been changed to an unordered list so a screen reader announces how many actions are available

I've also made sure the menu closes if a user Tabs away from the menu options, in which case the trigger button is _not_ auto-focused (since the user is moving away from the menu options, we don't want to steal focus back)

### Some additional context

Dropdowns as a whole are going to be looked at in #12297. I've tried to avoid any hasty abstractions here, so when we pick up that issue we can look at the bigger picture.

## Related Tickets & Documents

Closes #12250

## QA Instructions, Screenshots, Recordings

- Start a chat in `/connect` (you may need to set up your local instance to have some mutual follows to do so)
- Write a message and send to the chat
- I found I needed to reload the page to see my sent message (not sure at the moment if that's just a problem for me locally, but mentioning just in case!)
- Check that if you hover with a mouse towards the right hand side, you can see the 'three dots' menu appear next to your message
- Check that you can click the menu for it to open
- Check that you can close the menu with Escape key
- Check that you can Tab to the menu button, and it's visible when focused
- Press Enter to open the menu and check that the first item (Edit) is focused
- Check you can Tab to the second item (Delete)
- Check that pressing Escape closes the menu and refocuses the button with the three dots
- Check that if you re-open the menu with the keyboard, and tab _past_ the final option, the menu closes but doesn't place focus on the three dots button
- Check that when you focus on the three dots button with a screen reader on, that it's announced as "expanded" when the dropdown is open, and "collapsed" when it's not (exact behaviour may vary with different screen readers/browsers)
- Check that even when the three dots button isn't currently visible, that it's exposed to screen readers (e.g. in the rotor)
- Log out, and log in as the chat recipient, and check the same behaviours hold true for the "three dots" button on someone else's message (in which case 'Report abuse' is the only option in the popup)

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20773163/118838785-e083dd00-b8bd-11eb-96f3-0b64afd91c6b.mp4



### UI accessibility concerns?

Covered in the above test steps
